Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Civic life: news, government & the law

propose verb

put forward terms, a plan or a motion

also proposal, put forward, make a proposal, propose a motion, propose a law, motion, make a motion, approve a motion, oppose a motion, on my motion, bill (a law), decide (of the senate), vote (of a senator), bill (a proposed law), bill (parliament)

classical

Cic. Off. 2.73: cum lēgem agrāriam ferret
Traupman 180, 188: lēgem ferre, propose a law; pācis condiciōnēs ferre, propose terms of peace

ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum

verb, irregular; with condiciōnem, lēgem, rogātiōnem · Conjugation on Wiktionary

propose (terms, a law, a bill)

Lewis & Short: condiciōnem ferre, to proffer terms; lēgem ferre, to propose a law. A friendly suggestion is suādeō or auctor esse (see suggest).

Other words

  • condiciō, condiciōnis f. — a proposal, the terms offered

    noun, third declension · classical · Cic. Att. 7.14.1: probāta condiciō est · Declension on Wiktionary

    Condiciōnem ferre, accipere, repudiāre: to make, accept, reject a proposal. Also a proposal of marriage (see propose, ask someone to marry).

  • cēnseō, cēnsēre, cēnsuī, cēnsum — propose, move (in a meeting)

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 1.16: prīmum igitur ācta Caesaris servanda cēnseō; Traupman 179, 181, 402 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    A senator’s word when asked his view: “I move that …”, with a gerundive or an accusative and infinitive.

  • rogātiō, rogātiōnis f. — a bill, a law proposed to the people

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Balb. 33 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 178 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • sententia, sententiae f. — a motion (in a meeting); a view put forward

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 178: Quis in Crassī sententiam īvit?, Who supported Crassus’ proposal?; Traupman 179 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • referre (ad senātum) dē (+ abl.) — make a motion regarding, lay a matter before the senate

    also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 1.20: refer, inquis, ad senātum (Lewis & Short s.v. referō); Traupman 348 · Wiktionary

Examples

  • probāta condiciō est, sed ita ut ille dē iīs oppidīs quae extrā suam prōvinciam occupāvisset praesidia dēdūceret

    the proposal was accepted, but on condition that he withdrew his garrisons from the towns he had seized outside his provinceCic. Att. 7.14.1

  • prīmum igitur ācta Caesaris servanda cēnseō

    first, then, I move that Caesar’s acts be upheldCic. Phil. 1.16

  • mē referente

    on my motionTraupman 179

  • sententiam comprobāre

    to approve a motionTraupman 179

  • sententiae obsistere

    to oppose a motionTraupman 179

  • referre dē aliquā rē

    to make a motion about something (to put it before the senate)Traupman 179

See also suggest, propose, debate.
